title: Subsets
statement: Return every subset of distinct integers `nums`, including the empty subset. Sort each subset and sort the list of subsets.
hints: Every element is either in the subset or out of it. That is 2^n choices.
A depth-first walk that branches on include and exclude builds each subset once.
Bit masks from 0 to 2^n - 1 encode the same choices. Bit i selects nums[i].

approaches.name: Cascading copy
approaches.explanation: Start from [[]]. For each number, duplicate every existing subset and append the number.

approaches.name: Backtracking
approaches.explanation: The output dominates memory. The recursion depth is n.

editorial: The include/exclude recursion is the decision tree of the power set. Record a copy of the path at every node, or only at the leaves if you branch on both choices down to the end. Sorting the input first makes the emitted subsets comparable across implementations.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def subsets(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    nums = sorted(nums)
    out: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []

    def dfs(i: int) -> None:
        if i == len(nums):
            out.append(path[:])
            return
        dfs(i + 1)
        path.append(nums[i])
        dfs(i + 1)
        path.pop()

    dfs(0)
    out.sort()
    return out
